chapter: Family background and the Tulsa music scene
title: His father today, and leaving Haskell at three
summary: He recounts calling his father, J. W. Simmons, and moving to Muskogee.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My father? John W. Simmons. And he goes by the name of J.W. He's alive, in Oklahoma City. Jive, henpecked. Incidentally, I called him last night and told him how henpecked he was. He says, "Is that what you call me, boy?" I say, "Yeah." Say, "What you want me to do?" I say, "I want you to be a man." "Well, if I was you and you was me, I wouldn't talk to my father like that." I said, "I'm not talking to you like a father," I said, "I'm talking to you man to man," I said. "Like, I can't recognize you as a father," I said. "You haven't done anything for me in your life." I say, "My uncle has been more of a father to me than you," you know. I mean, I don't know what, why I did it, I mean, the devil made me do it. I just woke up, feeling that way, you know? This was during one of my getups yesterday, while I was trying to sleep. I called him in broad daylight, 3:00 o'clock.
You left Haskell when you were five.
And that was when you went to Muskogee.
